coreConcepts.term: play the ball as it lies
coreConcepts.definition: Hit the ball from the place where it stops. Do not move it to an easier place unless a rule allows it.
coreConcepts.whyItMatters: This is a basic golf rule. It keeps the game fair because all players must accept the result of the shot.

coreConcepts.definition: The short, neat grass area on the course.
coreConcepts.whyItMatters: It is usually easier to hit from the fairway, so learners need to know this course area word.

coreConcepts.definition: The taller grass next to the fairway.
coreConcepts.whyItMatters: A ball in the rough is often harder to hit, but the player usually still plays it there.

coreConcepts.definition: The ball's resting place on the course.
coreConcepts.whyItMatters: The lie affects the next shot. A good lie is easier. A bad lie is harder. In golf, the lie is part of the test.

coreConcepts.definition: Permission to move the ball in a legal way under a rule.
coreConcepts.whyItMatters: Relief is an important exception to the usual rule. A player must know when moving the ball is legal.

coreConcepts.definition: One extra stroke added to the score.
coreConcepts.whyItMatters: Penalty strokes change the final score, so players must understand when they happen.

coreConcepts.definition: A ball position outside the legal course area.
coreConcepts.whyItMatters: If a ball is out of bounds, the player usually adds a penalty stroke and plays again from the previous place.

coreConcepts.definition: The rule system used in golf, made by the R&A and the USGA.
coreConcepts.whyItMatters: Players use the official rules to make correct decisions during play.

connectionMap.label: basic rule decision
connectionMap.explanation: The first decision starts after the ball stops. The player checks the resting place, then usually plays from that same place.

connectionMap.label: course area meaning
connectionMap.explanation: The fairway is short grass, so it often gives a simpler next shot.

connectionMap.label: course area meaning
connectionMap.explanation: The rough is taller grass, so the ball may sit deep and become more difficult to hit.

connectionMap.label: exception to the main rule
connectionMap.explanation: A difficult position alone is not enough. The player can move the ball only when a rule gives relief.

connectionMap.label: score change mechanism
connectionMap.explanation: Some actions add one extra stroke. This makes the total score higher.

connectionMap.label: out of bounds process
connectionMap.explanation: Out of bounds has a clear result. The player adds a penalty stroke and usually returns to the earlier spot.

connectionMap.label: rule authority
connectionMap.explanation: These organizations make the rules, so players follow one shared system.

connectionMap.label: review grammar pattern
connectionMap.explanation: This pattern helps Hiroko explain golf rules clearly. Example: You usually play it there unless a rule allows relief.

miniCaseStudy.scenario: A ball stops in the rough near a tree. The player wants to move it to the fairway because the shot is difficult.
miniCaseStudy.analysis: The main rule says to play the ball as it lies. The rough is a normal part of the course, so difficulty alone does not permit moving the ball. The player must first check whether a rule gives relief. If no rule gives relief, the ball stays there and the player plays from that spot. A correct answer uses both rule meaning and course vocabulary.
miniCaseStudy.takeaway: Do not move the ball just because the shot is hard. First check the lie, then check whether relief is allowed by a rule.

trackingChecklist.focus: Review core words: fairway, rough, lie, relief, penalty stroke, out of bounds
trackingChecklist.note: Say each word and give one short meaning in simple English.
Practice this sentence: You play the ball where it stops.
Compare fairway and rough with short sentences: The fairway is shorter. The rough is taller.
Practice the pattern usually plus unless: You usually play it there unless a rule allows relief.
Answer this clearly: What is a penalty stroke? It is one extra stroke added to the score.
Say the full action in order: out of bounds, penalty stroke, play again from the previous place.
Explain the main golf rule in two or three sentences without looking at notes.
